chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: 'Whoever performs Tawaf around the House and makes a mistake until he enters the eighth [lap], let him complete fourteen Shaws [laps], then let him pray two Rak'ahs.' What this report contains, and the report before it, from his saying 'he prays two Rak'ahs', is not contradictory to what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one makes a mistake during Tawaf and reaches the eighth lap?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the procedure for a pilgrim who loses count and proceeds to the eighth lap, mandating the completion of fourteen laps followed by the two rak'ahs of Tawaf prayer. The text explicitly notes the consistency of this ruling with previous narrations, reinforcing the jurisprudential principle of completing the ritual despite the error rather than restarting. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the validity of Tawaf even when minor counting mistakes occur, provided the pilgrim fulfills the required number of circuits.
